title: Dave Canales previews Packers matchup: 'We have to recapture our process'
headline: Damien Lewis and Akayleb Evans are day-to-day for Thursday at Green Bay; if Evans can't go, Marco Wilson is the likely replacement at corner.
summary: Canales framed the short week as a challenge: several players are day-to-day, and the staff will test them Tuesday to decide who can play Thursday night at Lambeau. He said the coaches are weighing who fits the game plan best, not just who is the logical next man up. Offensive line and cornerback depth both came up, with Canales naming Marco Wilson as a quicker, athletic option at corner if Evans is out. On the locker room, he described focus and intentionality after the loss, and stressed fundamentals, turnovers, and special teams as the reset. He expects the Packers to lean on the run after Carolina's recent run defense performance and says Jordan Love will still push the ball downfield. He called the 2025 win in Green Bay a useful template but said this is a different team. He also noted Josh Jacobs' return and said Carolina must tackle well and maintain leverage against him.

title: Matt LaFleur on the Panthers: 'We've got a great challenge ahead of us'
headline: Zaire Franklin is out for Thursday's Carolina game, Sean Rhyan is likely headed to IR, and Savion Williams is earning a bigger role as a downfield weapon.
summary: LaFleur said the Packers are working through injuries on a short week and that practices this week are mostly walk-throughs, with a short indy session planned. Zaire Franklin will not play Thursday. Sean Rhyan is likely heading to IR, though LaFleur said the team has more time before deciding. Travis Glover missed practice after a knee injury he suffered late in the last game, and LaFleur said he's hopeful for him. Josh Jacobs looked physical and tough in his return, but LaFleur acknowledged the run game has had breakdowns and said the problem falls on the whole unit. Kevin Zeitler is still ramping back up after missing the offseason and training camp, and he'll play when he's ready, with LaFleur saying he'd be ready if needed. LaFleur said Savion Williams has given the offense a spark, making key plays on third downs and playing as a physical presence. Kaleb Johnson's playing time depends on special teams and pass protection, not only his role as a backup. LaFleur described Carolina as a tough, well-coached defense, and said Bryce Young is playing well with plenty of weapons.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 26, 2026
headline: Saquon Barkley tweaked his back on an early 29-yard run and was on a pitch count, playing less than planned before exiting early in the second half.
summary: Sirianni said the run defense gave up a lot of yards Monday night because of a mix of coaching, execution, getting off blocks, and missed tackles, and he credited the Cowboys for a good game. He said the team reviews every missed tackle and will rep those fixes in practice, and he took responsibility for providing the tools. On the lack of pass pressure, he described multiple contributing causes rather than one, and said the staff will look for common themes. On Saquon Barkley, he said the team monitored him closely on a pitch count and put his health first, and that he came out early in the second half. Barkley tweaked his back on a 29-yard run, and Sirianni said he played less than initially expected but was productive when he touched the ball. Sirianni said playing without six day-one offensive starters is part of NFL life and not an excuse, and that depth players get development opportunities. Offensively, he cited efficient running, play action, tempo, red-zone finishing, and third-down conversions (he thought just over 40%) as positives that still need work. He also discussed leadership development for young players and shared the postgame message of consistency, growth, and gratitude, saying the division race is still wide open with ten games left.

injuries.detail: Tweaked his back on an early 29-yard run and was on a pitch count, leaving early in the second half; Sirianni said he was ready to play and was productive when he touched the ball.

signals.claim: Played less than the team initially planned after the back tweak and early-second-half exit, with a pitch count in place.
signals.note: A back tweak and pitch count raise questions about his workload and whether he will be fully unrestricted next week, which affects his volume for fantasy.
signals.quote: he definitely played a little less than what we initially thought.

topics.detail: Sirianni blamed a mix of coaching, execution, getting off blocks, and missed tackles for allowing many rushing yards, and said the team will drill tackling in practice.
Asked about season-long quick-pressure rates, Sirianni said there is no single cause and the staff will look for common themes to improve.
Positives included efficient run game, play action, tempo calls, and red-zone finishing, but third-down conversion (about 40%) still needs improvement.
The team played without six day-one offensive starters, which Sirianni framed as part of NFL life and an opportunity for depth players, not an excuse.
Sirianni said he works with captains and veterans on leadership development and leading by example, tailored to each player's situation.
He emphasized consistency, growth, and gratitude, said the division race is wide open with ten games left, and credited the Cowboys.
